# Security Checklist: ISK-0004 — Persistence Abstractions & PostgreSQL Foundation

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for tenant isolation, row-level security, the operator scope, database roles, credentials, TLS, and disclosure of connection detail are complete, clear, and consistent
**Created**: 2026-11-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Tenant Isolation

- [x] CHK001 - Is "tenant-owned table" defined by a criterion that can be read from the catalog, rather than by a list a new table could be left out of? [Clarity, Contract §Isolation 1, Research R5]
- [x] CHK002 - Are the row-level security policy expressions stated exactly for organization-owned and project-owned tables, covering both reads (`USING`) and writes (`WITH CHECK`)? [Completeness, Contract §Isolation 2]
- [x] CHK003 - Is it specified whether a project-scope unit may see its parent organization's organization-owned rows, and whether an organization-scope unit may see its projects' rows? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §SC-004, Contract §Isolation 2]
  - Decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-10: keep the current policy and state it. A project unit sees its own organization's organization-owned rows, and an organization unit sees no project-owned row. FR-006, SC-004, contract Isolation rule 5, and T029 now say so.
- [x] CHK004 - Is reporting a foreign row exactly as a missing row specified for every operation, including optimistic update and delete and a reference by ID? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006, Contract §Optimistic concurrency, Research R10]
- [x] CHK005 - Can the isolation requirement be measured with the repository predicate both present and omitted? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK006 - Are scope settings required to be transaction-local, and is the pooled-connection leak surface listed (settings, temporary tables, prepared state, locks)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §US3 scenario 5]
- [x] CHK007 - Do the requirements address SQL inside a unit changing its own scope settings, which row-level security trusts? [Gap, Contract §Known limits]
  - Fixed: nothing stopped repository SQL from calling `set_config('iskender.organization_id', …)` and switching its scope mid-transaction. The contract's known limits, research R21, and T031 now make the module-namespace check fail on `set_config` or an `iskender.` setting in a module namespace, and leave other routes to review.

## Scope Construction and the Operator Scope

- [x] CHK008 - Is it specified that a unit's scope comes only from attested sources, so a scope built from caller values cannot be expressed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Research R4]
- [x] CHK009 - Is the operator-scope refusal specified with its code, its timing (before any statement), and the row-level security result if the check is bypassed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK010 - Is the reverse case, a tenant-scope unit naming an operator table, specified? [Coverage, Research R6, Contract §Isolation 6]
- [x] CHK011 - Is the elevated operator operation reserved explicitly, with no API for it in this spec? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions, Contract §Left to later specs]

## Roles and Privileges

- [x] CHK012 - Are the runtime role's limits (owns nothing, no `BYPASSRLS`, not superuser, no DDL) stated as requirements that can be read from the catalog? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010, §FR-022, Contract §Isolation 7]
- [x] CHK013 - Is the split between migration and runtime identities specified, including that a data-plane process need not hold migration credentials? [Completeness, Spec §TR-9, Contract §Configuration]
- [x] CHK014 - Is the automated row-level security policy check specified both as a test and as a runner refusal? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, Research R5]

## Credentials

- [x] CHK015 - Is it specified that passwords exist only as `secretRef` values and reach the adapter only through the credential port, once per physical open, uncached? [Completeness, Spec §FR-031, Contract §Credentials]
- [x] CHK016 - Is the outcome defined both for a missing credential provider and for a registered one that fails? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-031, Contract §Failures]
  - Fixed: only a missing provider had an outcome. A provider that throws, for example because a secret is missing, would have fallen to "unexpected" and `core.internal`. The contract, research R8 and R17, and T012 and T039 now classify it as authentication failed, `persistence.unavailable`, with the probe reporting `authentication_failed` and none of the provider's exception text kept.
- [x] CHK017 - Is it stated that no production credential provider ships, and what that means for a production host until ISK-0021? [Clarity, Spec §TR-14, Contract §Credentials 2]

## TLS

- [x] CHK018 - Is the meaning of `require` defined precisely (chain and host-name verification), with its difference from libpq's `require` stated? [Clarity, Research R15, Contract §Configuration]
- [x] CHK019 - Is the private-CA limitation recorded as a known limit, with the CA bundle setting named as post-MVP? [Assumption, Contract §Known limits, Plan §Risks]
- [x] CHK020 - Is `disable` limited to `development`, with the validation error it gets elsewhere stated? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases, Research R15]

## Disclosure

- [x] CHK021 - Are all channels that must never carry connection detail named (probe results, errors, logs, metrics, traces), and the forbidden values listed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK022 - Is the canary requirement measurable: which values carry the canary and which channels are searched? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, Tasks T043]
- [x] CHK023 - Is it required that the driver's own logging and tracing stay off, since they carry SQL and connection detail? [Completeness, Research R18, Contract §Diagnostics]
- [x] CHK024 - Is it required that values never enter SQL text, so parameters cannot leak through statement text? [Completeness, Research R2]
- [x] CHK025 - Can each negative security scenario be traced to a requirement and a contract rule? [Traceability, Spec §Negative Security and Failure Scenarios, Contract §Threat model]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
